gen-fs-chubbo-gf-orbit: Chubbo looks like it was drawn with a marker tip, soft and inviting around every bend. And Orbit, a plain sans, keeps its curves open and its characters floating apart, so it handles the quieter work.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-trispace: Tight, confident, and built like a poster. Oswald packs its rows close and hits hard, while Trispace spreads its sans letters wide, with curves that open outward instead of curling in.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-anuphan: Chubbo's smooth, marker-tip curves give it a casual, inviting look with no snags at any bend. But shrink it down and that softness fades, whereas Anuphan, with big round bowls and clear gaps, holds up fine at size.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-tsukimi-rounded: Tsukimi Rounded fills the paragraph with round forms like open parentheses, a soft, featureless hum of sans. Oswald is the one that packs its rows tight and speaks up.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-montserrat-underline: Casual and inviting, Chubbo hands over to something sturdier. Montserrat Underline brings hollow-reed counters and a lowercase that looks oversized next to its capitals, so the two sit at different heights.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-tuffy: Oswald is confident and strong, its rows tightly knit. Tuffy follows with a pencil-sketch single stroke and a widely parted s, so the page goes from punchy headline to easy, contemporary text.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-nokora: Marker-tip curves give Chubbo its smooth, casual charm. Nokora brings the opposite energy, a plain sans with a wide-open s and a thick, dark stripe of lowercase running through every line.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-urbanist: Urbanist writes like a rolling-ball pen, one single-width trail that never curls shut. Oswald earns its keep big and short, where those tightly knit rows can show off their confidence.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-varela: Varela reads modern and approachable, with c shapes like a wide mouth and a t whose crossbar and stem share one width. Over a long passage, Varela keeps its lines holding their thickness, while Oswald stays confident up top.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Chubbo keeps its stems and arcs in lockstep, with a marker-drawn, inviting feel. Noto Sans Buhid, a plain sans, gives generous space between curve ends and stems, and its modern polish sits quietly beside that looseness.
